instruction: Save this webpage as a PDF to the Desktop, but only include pages 1 through 5.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully saved the current webpage as PDF to Desktop with no margins. Used Ctrl+P to open print dialog, expanded More Settings, changed margins to None, navigated to Desktop in file save dialog, and saved with default filename. Then verified file existence via Files app.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can use Ctrl+P for print dialog, navigate print settings (margins, layout, pages), use file save dialog to choose destination folder, interact with Chrome browser, search and open desktop applications
metadata.task_rationale: Tests the same print-to-PDF workflow but requires changing the page range instead of margins. The model demonstrated ability to navigate print settings; specifying a page range is a related interaction in the same dialog.
metadata.explanation: Task requires saving the webpage as PDF with only pages 1-5. Custom getter extracts page count from the saved PDF file. Custom metric checks that the file exists (0.5) and that the page count equals 5 (0.5).

scoring_breakdown.file_exists: 0.5 - PDF file exists on Desktop with default filename

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly fetches PDF from VM via env.controller.get_file(), writes to temp file, and uses PyPDF2/pypdf to extract page count — appropriate for verifying page range requirement
Metric correctly handles expected parameter for type='rule': accesses expected.get('expected_pages', 5) directly, consistent with get_rule returning rules dict
Both instruction requirements are verified: file existence on Desktop (0.5 points) and page count equals 5 (0.5 points)
Error handling is sound: getter returns error dict on failure, metric returns 0.0 on error or missing file
No postconfig needed since getter reads a saved file from disk, not UI state
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: The hardcoded PDF filename assumes Chrome's default naming from the page title. If the page title changes or Chrome formats it differently, the path may not match. Consider a glob-based approach to find PDF files on the Desktop as a fallback.
